text:
kevin: rolling up an experiment proposal — p95-driven token pacer per route/tier. want to validate whether lowering the per-request token budget for low-cost routes reduces p95 tail without hurting throughput.

kevin: plan is a canary with two knobs: dynamic_token_target and batch_window_ms per tier. start conservative.

tara: SGTM. curious about KV cache interaction — if we shrink token budget we might hurt prefix reuse and increase kernel switches. did you profile kv hit rates?

kevin: quick profiling on staging shows ~12% drop in KV hit ratio for short-chat routes when token_target reduced from 256->180. but effective latency p95 dropped ~60ms in steady-state. tradeoff looks plausible.

jules: do we have a config snippet so infra can spin the canary?

kevin: sharing sample canary config:

```
route: "chat.low"
tiers:
  - name: "free"
    dynamic_token_target: 180
    batch_window_ms: 6
  - name: "paid"
    dynamic_token_target: 230
    batch_window_ms: 4
canary: true
rollout: 5% nodes
```

anita: thanks. two requests: 1) add a kv_warmup=true flag for the canary so we can measure hit recovery curve; 2) emit p95 by route + kernel_switch_rate metric.

kevin: added both. we'll surface kernel_switch_rate as `runtime.kernel.switches_per_min`.

deploy-bot: canary created — 5% nodes in us-west2 for routes matching `chat.low` (id=cny-3245).

sam: quick heads-up — last time we reduced token targets we saw a perf regression for long-seq rerank jobs due to extra kernel handoffs. can we pin model variant for rerank routes to avoid the regression?

kevin: good catch. rerank routes are excluded from this canary (explicit in rollout matcher). will add a hard exclusion by tag.

tara: what observability to watch? suggested list: p95_latency_by_route, kv_hit_rate, kernel_switch_rate, batch_size_distribution, tokens_per_request, svc_error_rate. Also watch GPU utilization per node.

jules: raising one more: set up a short A/B eval with our critical prompt set (billing and auth flows) to ensure quality doesn't regress due to early cutoff.

kevin: added eval job `p95-pacer-canary-eval` to run against canary vs baseline every 10m. will abort rollout on quality regression >1% or p95 increase >10ms.

anita: timeline?

kevin: canary running now. check dashboards in ~12 minutes once steady-state. initial telemetry looks promising: p95 for chat.low down 48ms, kv_hit_rate -11% immediate but trending up after ~60s. kernel_switch_rate +3%.

sam: any logs of microbatch behaviour? want to see if smaller token budget causes more frequent microbatches and overhead.

kevin: attaching a short log excerpt from node-17:

```
[2026-03-18T12:05:10Z] req=3821 route=chat.low tokens=174 batched_with=5 kv_hit=true kernel=fp16_matmul
[2026-03-18T12:05:10Z] req=3822 route=chat.low tokens=32 batched_with=3 kv_hit=false kernel=fp16_matmul
[2026-03-18T12:05:11Z] req=3828 route=chat.low tokens=180 batched_with=7 kv_hit=true kernel=int8_fast
```

tara: looks like mixing kernels still happening (matmul vs int8_fast). the increased kernel switches are small but could compound under burst. can we bias kernel selection to prefer int8_fast for these routes?

kevin: we can add a kernel affinity hint in the runtime config per route. proposing `preferred_kernel: int8_fast` for paid & free but let runtime fallback.

anita: risks? if int8_fast has worse quality for some long tokens, we need eval gating.

kevin: agreed. eval job will check. if quality dips, we revert kernel affinity and try increasing batch_window_ms instead.

jules: FYI, infra saw slight uptick in GPU context switches ~2% on canary nodes. not alarming but tracking.

deploy-bot: canary metrics snapshot: p95(chat.low)=184ms (-48ms), kv_hit_rate(chat.low)=0.72 (-0.09), kernel_switch_rate=+3.1%, gpu_ctx_switch=+2.2%.

tara: recommend keeping canary at 5% for now, collect 1 hour of steady-state and then try 25% if no regressions. also schedule a short load test with synthetic burst pattern to verify tail behavior.

kevin: will do. thanks all — leaving thread open for more telemetry. :eyes:

anita: tagging @eng-sre for longer-term risk assessment before 25%

sam: :thumbsup: noting rollback plan as discussed.
